cards.note: The town of Abancay is surrounded by tall, brown mountains with sparse vegetation, visible from most parts of the city.

The gen 3 coverage near Andahuaylas is tricky. The landscape looks lush, similar to Cajamarca. The combination of very overcast skies, black gen 3 car, and tall eucalyptus trees is a good clue for this area.

Arequipa has a distinctive colonial-style architecture, with arched windows and small overhanging roofs. Many houses in the old-town are built from sillar, a white volcanic rock. This cobblestone pavement is also quite common in the city.
Cajamarca city can be identified by its abundance of northern-style roofs (overhanging with wooden supports) and white colonial-style architecture.
The town of Cusco has both red brick houses and white Spanish colonial-style buildings. It is surrounded by mountains. Buildings with orange or red tiled roofs are most common in Cusco region.
The city of Huanuco is surrounded by huge dark-green, barren mountains.
Huancayo can be recognized by the huge mountains surrounding the city, as well as its grid.
A good clue for Lima is overcast weather, as other coastal areas often have clear blue skies. Boulevard-type streets are also mostly only found in Lima.
Roads inside Iquitos have both the dark asphalt found on the road to Iquitos and concrete pavement. Transitions between these pavement types are often in poor condition.
Moquegua’s second-largest city, Ilo, is a somewhat hilly coastal city surrounded by sand dunes.
The city of Moquegua is surrounded by rocky, light-colored, dry mountains. These mountains are also a good way to recognize Moquegua region.
Cerro de Pasco is a very high-elevation mining town. The buildings have metal sheet roofs, and the town is surrounded by rugged, barren mountains.

Oxapampa features wooden elements reminiscent of architecture in the Alps (this type of architecture can only be found in Pasco and Junin). The town can also be recognized by the forested, tropical hills that surround it.
The towns of Piura and Sullana can most easily be recognized by the abbundance of these mesquite trees, which are less common in coastal regions south of it.
Juliaca is the largest town in the region and is flat, with a lot of red brick architecture. On gen 3 many of the roads inside the city are unpaved.
Tarapoto is the largest city in the region. It is mostly gen 4 and somewhat hilly. If you are in a large tropical city with visible mountains, it’s likely Tarapoto.
Tacna is flanked by huge sand dunes on both sides of the city.
The center of Pucallpa is gen 4. It is flat and well-paved. Check Pucallpa’s grid to verify. A similar-looking city is Yurimaguas, north of Tarapoto.
